questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: funny times

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked my abroad experience very much, and i loved the city Amsterdam. It reminds me a lot of home, and it was very easy to find new friends. I lived in a student housing, so through that i easily met a lot of people

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it very simple and easy, Both KU and UvA gave a lot of easy information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I lived in a student housing, so there was som RA's that helped with all the practical stuff

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got a offer through my host institution

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I chose to live further away from the center and prioritized the housing qualities. It was a very good decision and the metro was nearby. I met almost all my friends at my student building

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to chose courses from the catalogue in advanced, then get them confirmed from the home univiersity. Its was very easy and simple

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could easily just email or contact the university or international office if you had troubles or questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got accepted at social behavioral science, which is not what i study at home. But i stille got some interesting courses even though its not what i study at home.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just have in mind that the courses is different from the courses at KU

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very different from what i was used to. A very high study load, attendance and very hard exams. Dont go to amsterdam if you are not prepared to study a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The study load is very very high compared to KU. You have to read a lot and do a lot of presentations. Also the attendance part. You are not allowed to miss classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures was quite similar but the seminars was very interactive and you have to read the texts and understand them to follow along.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Gender and Sexuality Studies
Topic Always Connected: Key insights in youth, media and technology

Global Digital Cultures: Interdisciplinary Perspectives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global digital cultures was a very interesting course, the teaching was good and the lectures was also. You learned a lot of stuff i stille use now at my studies

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At my student housing there was a lot of social activities such at pub quiz, bar nights, pizza nights etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Buy a museumscard and try all of the museums experience in the City. Go to the markets and try the local dutch food. Also The vintage market (IJ-hallen)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Cocos outback, a nightclub/bar for international students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think Amsterdam reminds me a lot of Copenhagen, so i felt the culture was quite similar to ours.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt spend that much time with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I actually didn't find any big differences in the culture. I find it very easy to adapt in the city. The loxals are very good at speaking english also

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness, and their ability to speak english. Everybody in Amsterdami s very good at speaking english

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to study a lot!!
2. Be social with other international students
3. Try the local specialities and get a bike!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get used to bike if you not already are, Amsterdam is a biking city

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friendships ive got after the exhchange. Now i have good relations to people form all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was the part were i tore my ACL in the first week of my exchange. I got a lot of close friends quickly because of it. but i had to ask for help which im not normally good at

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
